text:
sre-bot: ALERT: autoscaler ceiling reached for cluster/gpu-pool-prod. desired_nodes=120 max_nodes=120. queue_depth=~4300 (10m), pod_pending=78. Throttling detected for gpu inference jobs. https://dash.redwood.internal/autoscale/gpu-pool-prod :rotating_light:

oncall-nikhil: Ack. I'm on it. Paging eng-platform and gpu infra owners. Raising severity to P1.

maria: On GPU infra — seeing AZ-a exhausted (all spot/ondemand capacity used), node bootstrap failures from cloud provider intermittently. pod events: many Pending (0/1 nodes available) with taint/selector mismatch on a subset. Paste of `kubectl describe pod` window:

```
# pending pod sample
Events:
  Type   Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----   ------            ----   ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m     default-scheduler  0/120 nodes are available: 120 max nodes reached.
```

maria: Also HPA targets are healthy, it's literally node pool ceiling.

jonah: Not seeing any new release in the last hour. Ingress shows a traffic spike from a batch customer (cid-54321) starting ~10m ago, rate +46%. Might be legitimate but amplified.

support-anya: We have 3 customer incidents opened reporting 429s/timeout errors: cid-54321 (high qps), cid-98765 (dedicated), cid-11223 (dev). Notified SLAs for dedicated customer. I'll start proactive comms.

alek: We can do an emergency manual cap raise on the autoscaler (cloud quota permitting). Options: 1) bump max_nodes to 160 temporary, 2) add an extra nodepool with different instance types to absorb backlog, 3) apply admission control to shed low-priority requests. Which do you want?

eng-platform: I can do #1 immediately if ops approves. Will open a short-lived change and keep rollout reversible. Need someone to own customer comms while I execute. Also will monitor costs — set tag to "incident-emergency".

oncall-nikhil: Do it. Prioritize customer availability. assign eng-platform to execute. Maria, can you validate node selectors and taints so new nodes accept pods?

maria: Yes validating. Current issue: some pods require instance-type:gpu-v3 and new nodepool would be gpu-v2. We should only schedule non-latency-critical workloads to gpu-v2. I'll patch tolerations for best-effort queue to land on gpu-v2, not dedicated customer pods.

deploy-bot: CHANGE_REQUEST: Manual autoscaler increase initiated by eng-platform. change_id=CR-20625-87. Action: set autoscaler.maxNodes=160 for nodepool gpu-pool-prod. ETA: ~180s to request nodes.

eng-platform: Running command: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling ... --max-num-replicas=160` (abbrev). Submitted. Quota check passed for +40 nodes.

maria: New nodes requesting now. Cloud reports provisioning. Kube nodes moving from 120 -> 137 in last 90s. Patch applied to best-effort deployments: added toleration and lower priorityClass.

jonah: I'm seeing backlog drain rate improving: queue_depth 4300 -> 2100 in 3m. Latency p99 for serving dropping from 4.2s -> 2.1s. Good sign.

support-anya: Notifying impacted customers: cid-54321 message: we observed capacity throttling, temporary mitigation in progress, ETA to resolution ~10-15m. Will update.

alek: Quick note — we need an on-call handoff in ~20m. Nikhil, can you rotate to incident manager and hand off to me for post-incident follow-ups?

oncall-nikhil: Yep handing incident to alek in 20m. Alek will take lead for next 1h. :thumbsup:

eng-platform: New nodes converged. cluster nodes=160. Pods scheduling, backlog decreasing to 500. I recommend leaving max_nodes at 160 for the next 30m while we observe, then step down to 130 then to configured baseline. Initiating graceful scale-down policy after 30m.

maria: Confirming dedicated customer pods are on gpu-v3 nodes only. Best-effort jobs moved to new gpu-v2 pool. No taint leaks.

sara: Observability notes: added temporary alert to detect autoscaler=max for >5m and queue_growth>1000. Will add runbook link to incident channel.

support-anya: Customers updated. One dedicated customer asked for incident timeline and RCA — collecting details.

jonah: Post-incident action items I propose: - increase autoscaler headroom (10% buffer) - faster scale-up aggressiveness on queue spike - automated safety playbook to create temporary nodepool on hitting ceiling - better per-customer rate limiting for batch jobs.

alek: Agreed. I'll own action items and coordinate with infra/pm. Opening follow-up ticket: INC-20625-EMERG-RCA.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT_LOG: manual cap raise applied, nodes added, autoscaler.maxNodes changed 120->160 by eng-platform. change_id=CR-20625-87.

oncall-nikhil: Handoff: I'm switching to incident manager; alek you're lead. Alek, take 1st responder for next steps, I'll be available for escalation.

alek: Taking lead. Thanks Nikhil. I'll prepare a short customer-facing timeline and schedule RCA with infra + product.

maria: Follow-up immediate to-do: (1) add a guard to prevent spot eviction patterns from draining capacity, (2) validate cloud provider transient errors that delayed bootstrap.

sre-bot: RESOLUTION: capacity increased and backlog drained. Monitoring for 30m. Incident severity will be downgraded when all customer errors resolved and queue < 50 for 15m.

support-anya: Current status: 2 customers still reporting intermittent 429s but volume much lower. I'll keep them posted.

alek: Thanks team. We'll capture exact timing and mitigation steps in the RCA. Closing this thread when incident moved to postmortem.

sre-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. metrics link: https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/2062509876
